steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http module and the url module using the require() function.
steps.hint: Use require('module_name') to import Node.js built-in modules. You'll need both modules for creating a server and parsing URLs.
steps.seedCode: // Import the http and url modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The http and url modules are imported and ready to use in your code.
successCriteria: Both http and url modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Node.js modules. The http module will help create a server, and the url module will help parse query strings.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one module, but you need both http and url. Make sure to import both using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import both the http and url modules using require().

steps.title: Create the server instance
steps.instruction: Create a server instance using http.createServer(). Store it in a variable named 'server'.
steps.hint: Use the http module you imported earlier. The createServer method returns a server object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a server instance
const server = http.createServer();
steps.expectedOutcome: A server instance is created and stored in a variable named 'server'.
successCriteria: The server variable is declared and assigned the result of http.createServer().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a server instance that can handle HTTP requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using http.createServer() and storing it in a variable named 'server'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a server instance using the http module's createServer method.

steps.title: Define the request handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'requestHandler' that takes two parameters: 'req' (request) and 'res' (response).
steps.hint: This function will process all incoming HTTP requests to your server. Use the standard Node.js function signature for request handlers.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function named 'requestHandler' that can process HTTP requests and responses.
successCriteria: The 'requestHandler' function is defined with 'req' and 'res' parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the request handler function that will process all incoming HTTP requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named 'requestHandler' and accepts both 'req' and 'res' parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match what's needed. Remember to create a function named 'requestHandler' that takes 'req' and 'res' as parameters.

steps.title: Parse the request URL
steps.instruction: Inside your request handler function, use the url module to parse the request URL and extract the pathname and query parameters.
steps.hint: Use url.parse() with the request url and set the second argument to true to parse query parameters into an object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler function will be able to extract the URL path and query parameters from incoming requests.
successCriteria: The request handler function uses url.parse() to parse req.url and extracts pathname and query parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully parsed the request URL. This allows you to examine the endpoint path and any query parameters sent by the client.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're parsing the URL correctly. Remember to use url.parse() with req.url as the first argument and true as the second argument to parse query parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: The URL parsing isn't quite right. You need to use the url module's parse() method on the request URL to extract the pathname and query parameters.

steps.title: Check for the feature flag parameter
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, check if the 'feature' query parameter exists in the parsed URL object. Use an if statement to verify the parameter is present.
steps.hint: You can access the query parameters from the parsed URL object using the query property. Check if the 'feature' property exists on that object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will be able to detect whether the 'feature' query parameter was provided in the request URL.
successCriteria: The code includes an if statement that checks if parsedUrl.query.feature exists.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the check for the 'feature' query parameter. This validation ensures your endpoint can respond appropriately to requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking the 'feature' property specifically on the parsedUrl.query object. The if statement should verify this parameter exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: The check for the 'feature' query parameter isn't quite right. Remember to access the query parameters from the parsed URL and check if the 'feature' property exists on that object.

steps.title: Look up the feature flag value
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, after checking for the 'feature' query parameter, look up the feature flag value from the featureFlags configuration object using the feature name.
steps.hint: Access the featureFlags object using bracket notation with the featureName variable to get the boolean value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The requestHandler function now retrieves the feature flag's boolean value from the configuration object based on the query parameter.
successCriteria: The feature flag value is accessed from the featureFlags object using the featureName variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully looked up the feature flag value from the configuration object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're accessing the featureFlags object with the featureName variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to retrieve the feature flag's boolean value from the featureFlags object using the feature name from the query.

steps.title: Handle missing feature flags
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, after looking up the feature flag value, add an if statement to check if the featureName is not found in the featureFlags object and return a 404 error response.
steps.hint: Use the in operator or hasOwnProperty to check if the property exists in the featureFlags object. If it doesn't exist, set the response status code to 404 and end the response with an error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will now properly respond with a 404 error when a requested feature flag doesn't exist in the configuration.
successCriteria: The requestHandler function includes an if statement that checks if featureName is not in featureFlags and returns a 404 response with an error message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling for missing feature flags. The server will now respond appropriately when users request non-existent flags.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your if statement properly checks if the feature flag doesn't exist and returns a 404 status code with an error message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't properly handle missing feature flags. You need to add an if statement that checks if the requested feature flag doesn't exist in the featureFlags object and returns a 404 error response.

steps.title: Return the feature flag evaluation result
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, after handling missing feature flags, set the response headers to 'application/json' and send a JSON response containing the feature flag name and its enabled status.
steps.hint: Use res.setHeader() to set 'Content-Type' to 'application/json', then use res.end() with JSON.stringify() to send the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will now properly format and send JSON responses with feature flag evaluation results.
successCriteria: The response headers are set to 'application/json' and a JSON object containing the feature flag name and enabled status is sent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the JSON response for feature flag evaluations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're setting the 'Content-Type' header and using JSON.stringify() to send the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The response isn't properly formatted as JSON. Check that you're setting headers and sending a stringified JSON object.

steps.title: Start the server and listen for requests
steps.instruction: Call server.listen() to start the server on port 3000 and log a message when it's ready.
steps.hint: Use server.listen(port, callback) to start the server. The callback should log a message like 'Server running on port 3000'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start and listen for incoming HTTP requests on port 3000.
successCriteria: server.listen() is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully started the server. It's now ready to accept requests on port 3000.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling server.listen() with both the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't starting correctly. Check that you're calling server.listen(3000, callback) with the correct syntax.
